keys.statement: A first go/no-go on reactive distillation needs only relative volatilities, the equilibrium constant and the kinetics, read against the authors' applicability maps. The maps are for A + B to C + D with product C the lightest and product D the heaviest.

plain.title: Go or no-go on reactive distillation from three inputs: volatilities, equilibrium constant, kinetics
plain.when: You decide early whether reactive distillation is worth a rigorous study, for a reaction A + B to C + D with C the lightest and D the heaviest component.
plain.do: Read the relative volatilities, the equilibrium constant and the kinetics against the applicability maps of Muthia et al. 2018 (reflux ratio against stages) before any rigorous simulation.
plain.why: Generic maps for this reaction class show where a feasible column exists.
plain.check: The maps are about +/-30% for real systems: confirm a go with a rigorous simulation.

decisions.obstacle: Deciding early whether reactive distillation is worth a rigorous study.
decisions.mechanism: Generic maps of reflux ratio against stages.
decisions.operation: Screen with the maps before rigorous simulation.

keys.statement: A smaller equilibrium constant needs more reactive stages and a higher reflux ratio. In the base case at K = 0.01 the minimum is 22 stages and the minimum reflux ratio 11.

plain.title: Small equilibrium constant: expect more reactive stages and higher reflux
plain.when: The reaction's equilibrium constant is small.
plain.do: Allow more reactive stages and a higher reflux ratio.
plain.why: The products must be removed more completely on each stage.
plain.check: Compare your stage count and reflux with the map for your equilibrium constant.
plain.result: In the base case of Muthia et al. 2018, at K = 0.01 the minimum is 22 stages and the minimum reflux ratio 11.

decisions.mechanism: Products must be removed more completely on each stage.
decisions.operation: Allow more reactive stages and reflux.

keys.statement: When the light product is close in volatility to a reactant (relative volatility 1.2 instead of 2), the feasible region shrinks. At K = 0.01 the reactive stages needed rise from 28 to 64.

plain.title: Light product close in volatility to a reactant: the feasible region shrinks
plain.when: The light product is hard to separate from a reactant.
plain.do: Check the product-reactant relative volatilities first.
plain.why: The reactant leaves with the product unless the separation is sharp.
plain.check: Compute the light product's relative volatility against each reactant with your property method.
plain.result: At K = 0.01, a relative volatility of 1.2 instead of 2 raised the reactive stages needed from 28 to 64.

decisions.obstacle: A product hard to separate from a reactant.
decisions.mechanism: Reactant leaves with the product unless separation is sharp.
decisions.expected_change: Realistic stage count or a no-go.

keys.statement: If the Damkohler number divided by the equilibrium constant is at least 5, a kinetically limited column has the same configuration as at equilibrium; at 2 or more it is within 10%. Use this to set catalyst hold-up and residence time.

plain.title: Slow reaction in a reactive column: size the catalyst hold-up so Da/K is at least 2 to 5
plain.when: The reaction is kinetically limited and may need more reactive stages.
plain.do: Size catalyst hold-up and residence time so the Damkohler number (reaction rate relative to flow rate) divided by the equilibrium constant is at least 2 to 5.
plain.why: With enough hold-up the reaction behaves as at equilibrium: at Da/K of 5 or more the configuration equals the equilibrium one, at 2 or more it is within 10%.
plain.check: Compute Da/K from your kinetics, hold-up and feed rate.

decisions.obstacle: Slow reaction may need more reactive stages.
decisions.mechanism: Enough hold-up makes the reaction effectively at equilibrium.
decisions.operation: Size catalyst hold-up so Da/K is at least 2 to 5.

keys.statement: Avoid designs close to minimum stages or minimum reflux: near minimum stages the column is short and wide, near minimum reflux tall and slim, and catalyst use is lowest in between.

plain.title: Reactive column: stay away from both minimum stages and minimum reflux
plain.when: You choose the stage count and reflux of a reactive column and catalyst cost matters.
plain.do: Choose a configuration between the two limits.
plain.why: Near minimum stages the column is short and wide, near minimum reflux tall and slim. Catalyst volume follows diameter and reactive height, and is lowest in between.
plain.check: Compute the catalyst volume at a few points along the stages-reflux curve.

decisions.obstacle: Catalyst cost depends on column shape.
decisions.mechanism: Catalyst volume follows diameter and reactive height.
decisions.operation: Choose a configuration between the two limits.
